newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Netherlands' Zalm says no geographic bias for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Netherlands' Zalm says no geographic bias for EMU.

text.p: Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm, criticised earlier this month for saying some EU states should not be in the first wave of a single currency, said on Monday there would be no geographic bias in deciding members.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Zalm said that meeting the strict tests for qualifying for the euro would be the deciding factor.
"I think that the criteria should be applied strictly," he said. "We'll see which countries fulfil the criteria. There is no geographical discrimination whatsoever."

Zalm told reporters at the beginning of the Dutch European Union presidency earlier in January that he believed some countries should not try to force their economies to be ready for economic and monetary union (EMU) on January 1, 1999.

His comments were taken in some quarters as a slap to Spain, Portugal and possibly Italy. All three countries have been forcing the pace to try to get their budget deficits below three percent of Gross Domestic Product.
Zalm, who chairs meetings of EU finance ministers under the Ducth presidency, said in the interview that countries that did not make the grade in the first wave would have plenty of other chances.
"If you're not in the first group, you have the next year and the year after to enter based on the same criteria," he said.
"More countries than the first grouping will be in European monetary union before we start circulating coins and notes," he said.
Euro coins and notes are to become legal tender in participating countries in 2002.
